name: Vitis

project_scope.selection_mode: B025 strict review + B144 source-status reconciliation
project_scope.note: All four have canonical records. V. cinerea and V. palmata retain scientific range HOLDs. V. cinerea var. helleri maps to V. berlandieri.

study_strategy.warning: Do not call a Central Texas Heller's grape Vitis cinerea just because an app uses a broad species concept. Flip the leaf, inspect branchlets, and keep the berlandieri/helleri taxonomic reconciliation in mind.

quick_key.if: broad heart- to kidney-shaped leaves with dense white-to-rusty wool hiding the lower surface; large dark berries
lower leaf surface remains visible, sparsely webby/hairy to nearly glabrous; branchlets slightly angled; ripe berries conspicuously glaucous in short compact clusters
quick_key.then: Vitis berlandieri — canonical PASS; includes source-name V. cinerea var. helleri

quick_key.if: strict cinerea concept with angled branchlets densely short-hairy plus cobwebby; lower leaf remains visibly gray/green; small slightly glaucous berries
uniformly red/purplish-red/chestnut branchlets and usually deeply 3–5-lobed leaves with long-pointed lobes; lower surface essentially glabrous

comparison_matrix.cinerea: Blade visible, gray-green, short-hairy and webby

look_here_first: Find a tendril opposite a leaf. Flip a mature leaf to inspect underside hair density, then compare current-year branchlets and intact ripe berries.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched mature leaf underside macros of all four species
Same-age branchlet macros showing hair architecture
Intact berry clusters with ruler and undisturbed wax bloom
Matched whole leaves documenting lobing variation
overlap_cautions: Mustang grape can develop deeply lobed leaves on vigorous shoots.
Berry wax can rub off; avoid identification from bloom alone.
V. cinerea and V. palmata are canonical but remain range HOLDs.
Source-name V. cinerea var. helleri is represented by V. berlandieri.
